headline: Ben Bernanke Joins Anthropic Oversight Trust
summary: Former Federal Reserve Chair and Nobel laureate Ben Bernanke has been appointed to Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust, an independent body overseeing the responsible development of advanced AI. His economic expertise will guide the company's approach to AI's
details: Former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke has joined Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT). This independent body is tasked with ensuring Anthropic's mission of responsible AI development for humanity's long-term benefit.

Bernanke, a Nobel Prize winner in Economic Sciences, led the Federal Reserve from 2006 to 2014, navigating the 2008 global financial crisis. His academic work focused on financial crises and the Great Depression.

Dr. Bernanke stated that AI's potential is enormous, and its outcome depends on the institutions built around it. He is honored to contribute to Anthropic's unique governance structure to ensure benefits outweigh risks.

Anthropic Co-Founder Daniela Amodei highlighted Bernanke's career, from studying economic disruptions to steering the world's largest economy through one. His judgment will be crucial in anticipating AI's effects on workforces and economies.

As a Public Benefit Corporation, Anthropic balances commercial success with social good. The LTBT provides an independent check on the company's AI development and deployment, with Trustees chosen for diverse expertise and holding no equity.
Neil Buddy Shah, Chair of the LTBT, emphasized Bernanke's leadership and sound judgment during the 2008 financial crisis. This standard is sought for Trustees as AI's impact grows.
The LTBT can appoint Anthropic board members and advises leadership on AI's risks and societal impacts. Bernanke will lend his insight to economic research, particularly how AI changes the economy.
Bernanke joins existing Trustees Neil Buddy Shah, Richard Fontaine, and Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar. Their collective experience spans global health, national security, law, policy, and economics.
